claim.markdown_says:
Mro:
16A40-16A5E, 16A60-16A69 Multani:   (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 49319) ... then page-1219 opens with the bare line '11280-11286, 11288, 1128A-1128D, 1128F-1129D, 1129F-112A8' with no label
claim.why_it_matters: The 'Multani:' label from the top of PDF page 1189 is concatenated onto Mro's range line; Multani's ranges are orphaned at the head of the next page.

verdict.reasoning: Independently confirmed against 300 dpi renders of both pages, including a 1.4x upscaled crop of the bottom 20% of p1218 and the top 20% of p1219 read glyph by glyph. PDF page 1218 (printed folio 1188) ends its UCS script-range list with exactly two lines, 'Mro:' then '16A40-16A5E, 16A60-16A69', followed by roughly a fifth of a page of whitespace and then the footer '1188  (c)ISO/IEC 2023' and the licence line. There is no 'Multani:' token anywhere on PDF page 1218. PDF page 1219 (printed folio 1189) opens, under the running head 'ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)', with 'Multani:' on its own line, then '11280-11286, 11288, 1128A-1128D, 1128F-1129D, 1129F-112A8', then 'Myanmar:'. The markdown breaks that pairing exactly as claimed: specs/ISO_COBOL.md:49318 reads 'Mro:', :49319 reads '16A40-16A5E, 16A60-16A69 Multani:' as one line, the page-1219 anchor/heading/running-head occupy :49321-:49323, and :49325 is a bare '11280-11286, 11288, 1128A-1128D, 1128F-1129D, 1129F-112A8' carrying no label. Both of the claim's quotations are accurate and neither source is misquoted. I considered and rejected the 'page-break furniture / line wrapping' defence: no glyphs are lost and linear reading order is preserved, but the entire semantic content of this table is the label-to-range binding, and here that binding is broken in both directions at once - Mro's range line acquires a spurious trailing 'Multani:' token, and Multani's range list is orphaned from its name. Any line-oriented consumer extracting script ranges mis-parses two adjacent entries, and page 1218's transcription contains a token the PDF does not print on that page while page 1219's transcription omits one it does. That is a content-attribution defect, not formatting. 'structural' is the correct severity: record boundaries are corrupted, no characters are missing. Context: this sits in Annex E.3.3 item 5) 'Characters permitted in user-defined words', so the label-to-range binding is the substantive payload. The claim's only inaccuracy is cosmetic - it heads the finding with the PDF index (1218) but names the following page by its printed folio ('p1189'); PDF page 1219 == printed folio 1189.
verdict.corrected_description: CONFIRMED, with one cosmetic correction to the page numbering. At the 1218->1219 PDF page boundary the newline separating the last range line of page 1218 from the first label of page 1219 is collapsed to a space, gluing the next entry's label onto the previous entry's range: specs/ISO_COBOL.md:49319 reads '16A40-16A5E, 16A60-16A69 Multani:' where the PDF has '16A40-16A5E, 16A60-16A69' as the terminal body line of PDF page 1218 (printed folio 1188) and 'Multani:' as the first body line of PDF page 1219 (printed folio 1189). Consequently the page-1219 markdown block opens at :49325 with an unlabelled '11280-11286, 11288, 1128A-1128D, 1128F-1129D, 1129F-112A8'. No text is lost and reading order is preserved; the defect is the broken label-to-range pairing, which corrupts the Mro and Multani entries of the Annex E.3.3 UCS script-range table. NOTE - this is not a one-off. The identical newline-to-space collapse occurs at 19 page boundaries across this transcription; a scan for a range line ending in a glued 'Name:' token matches specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 40182, 40235, 40403, 40454, 40506, 40558, 40610, 40772, 40824, 40876, 40928, 40981, 49030, 49087, 49207, 49263, 49319, 49374 and 49431 (Ahom, Buhid x2, Kaithi, Linear_B, Miao, Old_Italic, Rejang, Gunjala_Gondi, Khojki, Mongolian, Sharada, Brahmi, Deseret, Kannada, Lydian, Multani, Old_Turkic, Sinhala). Sibling verdicts already logged for pages 1213, 1214, 1216, 1217 and 1219 record the same defect. The remedy is a single sweep re-splitting every one of those 19 lines at the label boundary and moving the label into the following page block, not 19 separate single-line patches.
